newsitem.title: BULGARIA: GOLDMAN SACHS SAYS BULGARIAN REFORM ON RIGHT PATH.
newsitem.headline: GOLDMAN SACHS SAYS BULGARIAN REFORM ON RIGHT PATH.

text.p: The chairman of global investment firm Goldman Sachs, Peter Sutherland, said on Tuesday he supported reform polices launched by Bulgaria's interim government, which came to power a month ago.
"The clear direction that is being taken by the government accords completely with the views which we would have," Sutherland told reporters after meeting Bulgarian President Petar Stoyanov.

"We offered some advice as to how this can best be moved forward, both in terms of supporting state finances and in terms of developing the privatisation process," said Sutherland, who is also former chairman of the World Trade Organisation.

Economists said that internatinal investment houses including Goldman Sachs have offered bridge loans once a clear reform policy is in place. They are also interested in privatisation deals including debt-for-equity swaps.
Bulgaria's caretaker government, in power until after parliamentary elections on April 19, is struggling to win foreign funding to pay huge foreign debts and secure vital imports like grain and fuel.
The interim cabinet, currently in talks with the International Monetary Fund for a new reform and funding arrangement, has pledged to speed up privatisation and liberalise pricing and trade policy.
The government hopes to sell off 16 major state enterprises by end-March in a move to raise desperately needed cash. -- Elisaveta Konstantinova, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
